newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Air Mauritius forecasts 96/97 profit slump.
newsitem.headline: Air Mauritius forecasts 96/97 profit slump.

text.p: National carrier Air Mauritius on Tuesday forecast an operating profit slump to 60 million rupees ($2.98 million) for the financial year ending 30 March 1997 from 610 million rupees in 1995/96.
Airline Chairman Nash Mallam-Hassam blamed the poor results for this financial year on extraordinary circumstances which affected the company's performance.
"This financial year is a oneoff, a flash in the pan," Mallam-Hassam told reporters.
He blamed the results mainly on a rise in fuel costs, the biggest cost component of the company, and which was exacerbated by a drop in the rate of the rupee versus the dollar in 1996.
"There was an 18 percent increase in price (of fuel) and an 11 percent rise in the rupee-dollar exchange rate," he said.
He added that Air Mauritius fuel bill for 1996/97 was estimated at 900 million rupees, 200 million rupees higher than it would have been without the exceptional items.
Mallam-Hassam took office in mid-February, replacing Sir Harry Tirvengadum who left to take up the post of chief executive at multi-national carrier Air Afrique.
"Indications show that (1996/97) profit will be of the order of 60 million rupees. This is the company I am taking over. This is where I start," he said.

He also blamed the results on higher dollar denominated debt servicing expenses, short term leasing of aircrafts, diminishing cash reserves due to capital disbursements and interests receivable on the reserves and an airbus aircraft being grounded after a fire exploded in one of its landing gears.
"It has been like lightning striking in the same place several times over," Mallam-Hassam said.
He pledged to get Air Mauritius profits back on track and aimed at a one-billion-rupee level within the next five years.

"We have to get out of the troubled waters first. Profit might be of 250 million rupees next year, 500 million rupees the year after, then one billion rupees in the 3rd or 4th or 5th year," he said but gave no further details. ($1=20.1565 Mauritian rupees).
